engine_facts_verified.stored_totals_reproduce: Q01-Q09 recomputed from their stored Arabic; all nine match texts.json exactly.
engine_facts_verified.chain_total_is_well_defined: Verified: the sum of member totals equals the total of the concatenated text. Q01+Q02+Q03+Q04+Q05+Q06 = 67563 computed both ways. So a chain's abjad total can be produced either by summing steps or by concatenating and computing once; the two cannot diverge.
engine_facts_verified.diacritics_ignored: is_ignorable() drops U+064B-065F, U+0670, U+06D6-06ED and standalone hamza U+0621. Only the consonant skeleton contributes. Consequence: a transcription error in a VOWEL MARK cannot change an abjad total; only a wrong, missing or extra LETTER can. This narrows what Hafiz has to check, but does not remove the need to check.

structure_finding.preset_chain_reading: LARGELY CONFIRMED, WITH ONE STRUCTURAL CORRECTION.
structure_finding.confirmed: The booklet is not a bag of individual texts. p.4 and p.5 are explicitly NUMBERED, ORDERED lists (10 and 13 items), and p.3 instructs the reciter to recite 'the Ruqyah (see p.4 and p.5)' as one unit, 3 or 7 times. A prescribed sequence is exactly what this booklet publishes.
structure_finding.correction: The booklet does NOT organise into N independent affliction-to-sequence chains. It publishes ONE base sequence plus CONDITIONAL ADD-ON BLOCKS, each gated by a printed heading ('One can add the following if affected by magic', 'When praying on others, add the following'). The affliction sections (p.6 evil eye, p.8 magic and jinn) are mostly PROSE ADVICE and NON-TEXTUAL remedies, not text lists. Modelling them as flat independent chains would duplicate the base 18 steps five times over and hide the gating logic.
structure_finding.model_adopted: base + add-ons, with a materialised presets layer on top so the cleric still gets one-click loading.
structure_finding.second_correction: Not every step is talisman material. p.8 prescribes reciting the whole of Surah al-Baqarah, and pp.8-9 prescribe sidr baths, senna, cupping, olive oil, honey, black seed and zamzam. Steps therefore carry a talisman_suitable flag; a chain is not the same thing as a talisman payload.

open_questions_for_hafiz.question: When a chain step carries a repetition count (7x, 3x, 100x), should that step's abjad total be MULTIPLIED by the count, or should the count be carried alongside the total and never folded into it?
open_questions_for_hafiz.status: NOT DECIDED BY THIS PASS. Flagged for the scholar, as instructed.
case_for_multiplying: The count is printed as part of the prescription, not as commentary. '(7x)' sits inside the item, on the same line as the text.
If the talisman is a written record of a prescribed ACT, and the act is seven recitations, then the number representing the act is arguably seven times the number representing one recitation.
Numerological practice around amulets often works in multiples and grids, so a multiplied value may be the value a practitioner actually expects to see.
case_against_multiplying: Abjad is a property of the TEXT (its letters). Reciting a verse twice does not add letters to it.
The counts in this booklet attach to the ORAL act, not the text. p.3 applies '3 or 7' to the entire ruqyah, so multiplying would scale every step by a factor the cleric picks at recitation time.
The counts are not stable. p.3 says 'at least 3 or 7'; p.11 says 'at least 7 times if possible'. A talisman number that moves with the reciter's discretion is not a property of the text.

Direct evidence inside this single booklet: RB-P05-01 carries NO count on p.5 but '3x evening' on p.12; Q04/Q05/Q06 carry no count in the ruqyah chain but '3x morning & evening' on p.12. The same text would produce two different totals depending on which page it was loaded from.
scope-v1 decision 5 says the QR plus the abjad values ARE the talisman. Folding in a count introduces a second, non-textual variable into the thing that IS the talisman.
open_questions_for_hafiz.recommended_data_shape_regardless_of_the: Store abjad_total and repeat_count as SEPARATE fields and decide the presentation at render time. That keeps both rulings buildable without a data migration: if Hafiz rules multiply, the renderer multiplies; if not, it displays '1788 x7'. Do not bake a multiplied number into stored data ahead of the ruling.
